title: Transmitter zero or span error
summary: The transmitter delivers a valid signal that does not match the process: a constant error points to the zero, a growing error to the span.

sections.heading: Recognizing it
sections.body: The channel configuration matches the drawing and the signal is within range, yet the value disagrees with an independent reference. Check the error at two levels: the same difference everywhere is an offset (zero) error; a difference that grows with the level is a span error. A large offset also pushes the signal over range near the top or under range near the bottom.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Compare with a reference (sight glass, second instrument, calibrator), then recalibrate the transmitter's lower and upper range values. Do not hide a calibration error by changing the scaling in the program: the next replacement transmitter would then be wrong.

troubleshooting.effect: The measured value is offset from the process value
symptoms: Two measurements of the same quantity disagree
Over range near the top of the range
evidence: A reference agrees with the other measurement
The loop current differs from the expected current for the level
diagnosticMethod: Calculate the expected current from the transmitter range
repair: Recalibrate the transmitter zero and span
troubleshooting.explanation: Calibration belongs to the instrument; scaling in the PLC must follow the documented range.
